newsitem.title: USA: Compaq plans handheld "PC companion" device.
newsitem.headline: Compaq plans handheld "PC companion" device.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp said it would offer a handheld personal computer that acts as a mobile extension of Windows-based desktop and notebook personal computers.
Compaq the world's largest maker of personal computers, said it plans to offer the new type of computer in North America later this year and worldwide during 1997.

The devices, part of an emerging category of computers known as information appliances, will use Microsoft Corp's Windows CE operating system that is designed to work with the new breed of "PC companions," the company said.

"Compaq is establishing a new breed of companion-type products that are designed to help customers more efficiently access and manipulate the massive amounts of personal and corporate information existing on...PCs and networks," said Ed Olkkola, vice president of Compaq's Commumnications unit.
The devices would be sold for use by office workers or home consumers.

"Customers are telling us they need a single solution that will keep their business and personal data current and instantly accessible when they can't be at their desks," Olkkola. "Compaq is developing an indispensable business tool to collect, use and exchange information with a PC."

Compaq said the new products are the result of a partnership its formed with Microsoft in April 1993, in which they agreed to jointly develop, promote and sell products based on industry-standard technology.
